question: Two airtight jars of the same ground black pepper: one in a cupboard, one on a sunny sill. After months, the sill jar is…?
options: Just as hot as the other
answer: Noticeably less pungent. Piperine, the molecule that bites, has double bonds that light can twist into other shapes, isomers such as chavicine and isochavicine, which bite far less. A lid keeps out air and moisture, not light. Chemists tracked the twist in ground pepper in 2007: clear glass on a bright shelf slowly blunts it.
move: Before trusting a seal, ask which enemy it actually shuts out.
trap: Just as hot, because airtight storage is what keeps spices fresh.
source: J Agric Food Chem, 2007, piperine isomers
